summary: The video captures a hands-on workflow for turning drone footage into polished panoramas, with a focus on file selection, lighting control, and a sequence of advanced post-processing techniques. Topics include identifying unprocessed drone files, using half-light edge lighting to connect scene elements, handling flare, stitching panoramas with Lightroom/Photoshop, PTGui, and PanoVolo, and employing masking, texture enhancements, and color grading (including the 50-150 adjustment) to emphasize fall colors and water textures. The tutor demonstrates a water-only warp for dramatic stream details, a five-piece perspective warp workflow for 360 panoramas, and batch-processing pipelines (including an automated image processor and exporting to TIFF). The session also covers directional lighting on wildlife, cropping centers for 360s, and practical notes about sky stitching and exposure management. Explicit location mentions (Patagonia, Wellington) are noted, and several timestamps anchor the key techniques demonstrated.

sections.title: Identify unprocessed drone files and assess lighting
sections.description: Begin by noting the presence of post-processed drone files and the need to locate unprocessed ones to apply a consistent workflow.

sections.title: Half-light technique introduction
sections.description: Demonstrates the half-light approach: introducing light from the edge to create shadows, mid-tones, and a cohesive connection across the scene.

sections.title: Pano attempt, flare, and shot evaluation
sections.description: Discusses a panorama attempt that was ruined by flare and the decision to move on to alternative shots, highlighting flare as a practical constraint.

sections.title: Texture and HDR prep for dramatic depth
sections.description: Uses auto-HDR-like adjustments to add texture while maintaining color fidelity; emphasizes controlling shadows and detail for depth.

sections.title: Batch processing and 0182 panorama prep
sections.description: Shows batch-adjusting a series of RAW frames, exporting to a dedicated folder, and preparing for stitching (including 0182 panorama files).

sections.title: Sky matching and panorama stitching workflow
sections.description: Discusses differences between stitching tools and the importance of exposure matching across frames when assembling panoramas.

sections.title: Five-piece perspective warp for 360 panoramas
sections.description: Explains that 360 panoramas warp into five segments to correct bottom/top distortion; demonstrates aligning the middle and progressively warping top/bottom for natural results.

sections.title: Center-focused cropping and island masking
sections.description: Emphasizes centering the subject and masking adjustments to protect non-target areas (e.g., removing distracting islands or edges).

sections.title: 50-150 color adjustment and fall color pop
sections.description: Details a two-step color workflow: global saturation increase followed by selective color reduction/addition to isolate fall colors; uses 50-150 to make fall hues pop.

sections.title: Wildlife lighting and final touchups
sections.description: Applies directional lighting to wildlife subjects (e.g., sea lion), uses masking to isolate adjustments, and performs light dodges or micro-color tweaks to draw attention to the subject.
